The field and the console

What the outside operator adds

The distributed control system (DCS) shows transmitters; the field adds gauges, valves and machines.

In the fieldOn this unit
Local indications42 instruments with a dial
Valve positions59 valves, 16 modelled hand valves
Machinessix pumps: running lamp, standby
Levels to climbgrade to the column top, +30.2 m

Visual plant 3D tab of this operator training simulator (OTS).

Interactive · click a station

The round on the plot plan

The round starts at the west end of the pump row, climbs the column and S-101, crosses to S-201 and ends at the battery limit.

Interactive · step through the stations

The view from each station

Each station is a fixed camera at eye height: the same view every round, so a change is easy to see.

Interactive · click a control

How to move through the plant

Next follows the yellow arrows; the pad walks freely and you arrive within 1.8 m of a station.

Interactive · move along the round

What the round costs in metres

Walked so far
Climbed so far
Floor here

The column top is one long climb of about 30 m: the round visits it once, in the middle.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The round reads what the DCS cannot: local gauges, valve positions, machines.
  • Fourteen stations in a fixed order, from the pump row to the battery limit.
  • Each station is a fixed view at eye height; Next follows the floor arrows.
  • The column top is climbed once.

Part 2

What does the operator read at each station, and how exactly?

Part 2 · the plan

From a station to a written number

  1. What is at a stationequipment, instruments, valves
  2. Reading a local gaugethe close-up and its range
  3. How exact a reading must be2 % of the range, by eye
  4. Gauges by levelwhich indications live on which floor

Interactive · pick a station, click a marker

What to read where

The route is fixed; now what each station asks for.

Each marker is a tag with a job: a value to write down, a position to confirm, or a machine to listen to.

Interactive · read the dial

Reading a local gauge, and how exact it must be

Rounds sheet tolerance$|x-x_{plant}|\le0.02\,(x_{hi}-x_{lo})$
Plant value
Accepted band
Rounds sheet

A gauge read by eye is accepted within 2 % of its range: 0.3 bar on a 0–15 bar a medium-pressure (MP) steam gauge.

In the tab: ◀ Read

The close-up of PI-209

◀ Read logs “Read PI-209 = …”; ↩ Back returns to the station. Screenshot at design.

Interactive · pick a level

Which indications live on which floor

Most readings are at grade, +11.8 and +14.0; the column top carries three, so plan one climb.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Each station lists its tags: values to write, positions to confirm, machines to check.
  • The close-up shows the dial, its range and the floor it is read from.
  • A local reading is accepted within 2 % of the instrument range.
  • Readings concentrate at grade, +11.8 and +14.0.

Part 3

How are hand valves, tags and the rounds sheet checked?

Part 3 · the plan

Positions, names and the written sheet

  1. Three kinds of hand valveoperable, locked open, locked closed
  2. The hand-valve register16 modelled valves, their normal positions
  3. A pump line-upevery valve against its normal position
  4. Identificationreading a tag, then naming it blind
  5. The rounds sheet28 rows checked against the plant

Interactive · pick a valve

Operable, locked open, locked closed

Readings are numbers; valves are positions, and some may not be moved.

A car-sealed valve refuses to move in the tab: breaking a seal needs a permit, not a click.

Interactive · pick a valve

The sixteen modelled hand valves

Fourteen are normally open; two are normally closed (top-head vent and hotwell drain), and two carry a lock.

Interactive · click a valve at the hotwell

Checking a pump line-up at station 13

A line-up check compares every valve with its normal position before a pump is started or handed over.

Interactive · decode the letters

Naming a tag from what it does

The ISA-5.1 letters (International Society of Automation, ISA) name what is measured and what the device does; the line tells where.

Interactive · pick a stretch of the round

The rounds sheet: 28 rows

Every row is checked against the live plant when the sheet is handed in; at design all 28 rows read as below.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Hand valves are operable, locked open or locked closed; a lock is never clicked away.
  • The register gives each valve's normal position, line and sheet.
  • A line-up compares every valve with its normal position.
  • Tags are named from their letters and line; the sheet is checked against the plant.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the same round in the same order every shift.

2

Read every local gauge to within 2 % of its range.

3

Check each hand valve against its normal position.

4

Never break a seal without a permit.

5

Name a tag from its letters and its line.
